Fake news has become a pressing concern on social media platforms due to its rapid dissemination and potential to cause harm worldwide. Although machine learning models have been effective in detecting false information, especially when large amounts of labeled data are available, their performance significantly declines when they are applied to emerging events. This limitation creates a significant obstacle for the current methods in detecting false news on unexpected events. Furthermore, the fact that newly emerging events necessitate building a new model from scratch or retraining the existing one, which is often expensive, time-consuming and impractical in real-world settings. To address this challenge, an end-to-end fake news detection system called MetaFEND has been proposed, allowing it to learn about both general features of news content and specific details of individual events. This system leverages the strength of meta-learning and neural process methods, incorporating a module that enables the elimination of unnecessary information about specific events. Experiments conducted on real-world datasets collected from Twitter and Weibo showed that MetaFEND consistently outperformed the existing methods in detecting false information on both known and unknown events. Moreover, it demonstrated significant performance improvements over the current approaches on both datasets.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained significant attention due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A pair GCA is defined as a set of four square matrices with the property that the sum of the squares of their elements equals twice the number of elements raised to the power of the matrix size, minus the sum of the squares of the differences of their elements in all possible combinations. Similarly, a quadruple GCA meets the same condition for six square matrices. A method is introduced to construct a GC pair in an n-dimensional space from a (n+2)-dimensional GC pair. Another approach is presented to construct a GC pair in a 4d space with two 3x3 binary matrices that meet specific conditions. Additionally, it is found that a 4d GCA with the following sizes is unnecessary: two 5x5 matrices, three 7x7 matrices, and four 9x9 matrices. All previously known low-dimensional GC pair patterns are included in higher-dimensional patterns.

A cutting-edge, minimally invasive therapy called Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy (LITT) treats seizures caused by epilepsy in a specific brain area, the mesial temporal lobe. Evaluating the effectiveness of this treatment requires analyzing changes to the treated brain area after LITT, which can be achieved by accurately defining the treated region through image processing. Although deep learning techniques offer high precision in defining this region, training them requires a large amount of data which can be hard to obtain for a new and emerging treatment such as LITT. In response, this paper proposes an innovative framework called Progressive Brain Lesion Synthesis, consisting of multiple stages to artificially create more training data with various characteristics, thereby enhancing the precision of the therapy evaluation. Furthermore, the paper includes a design for encoding external information that can aid in training and improving segmentation results by integrating a condition and mask embedding block, resulting in better outcomes when compared to common image processing methods, according to experimental data.

Dimensionality reduction in high-dimensional data is effectively managed by a technique called feature extraction. Self-supervised learning's prominent method, contrastive learning, has gained significant interest recently. Our novel, all-encompassing framework integrates contrastive learning for both initial learning and subsequent learning, thereby enabling unsupervised feature extraction. A code repository containing the implementation details is available online at https://github.com/ghoussam/CEFE.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance on numerous language tasks. To further enhance the performance and capabilities of these models, there is a growing interest in structured knowledge infusion. This paper presents a method called SKILL, which integrates structured knowledge directly into language models. The knowledge is organized in a form of a graph, allowing the models to perform reasoning and drawing inferences. Our approach differs from traditional training methods that rely on large amounts of text data. In the experimental phase, we incorporated general knowledge from Wikipedia into our SKILL framework, utilizing a 13-billion parameter language model. The results showed significant improvements in various knowledge-based tasks. Notably, our approach outperformed existing methods that incorporate knowledge through text data. Our findings suggest that structured knowledge infusion is more effective.

A nonlinear interaction occurs between electromagnetic fields in quantum electrodynamics, resulting in vacuum polarization. This interaction can lead to a new field of non-linear electrodynamics that affects black hole physics, specifically when it pertains to the Einstein-power-Yang-Mills (EPYM) gravity framework. We examine the relationship between an observable, shadow radius, and a first-order phase transition in a nonlinear, charged AdS black hole within the EPYM gravity context. Analyzing this connection, we identify conditions that allow for non-monotonic behavior among shadow radius, horizon radius, and temperature. Furthermore, we observe that the phase transition temperature can vary based on the value of an external magnetic field. These results suggest that the shadow radius is an effective indicator of black hole physics, capable of revealing phase transition information that is not accessible through thermal radiation or the disk-jet system.

Reconstructing a quantum state of continuous-variable systems like the radiation field is complicated and has several challenges, especially when trying to observe non-classical correlations and synchronization phenomena. Multiple methods have been proposed for accessing different aspects of a state, including its entanglement, as well as the Wigner function, which can be used to determine if a state meets the criteria for a Gaussian state. In the microwave cavity regime, non-linear effects such as parametric amplification or the use of additional measurements like homodyne detection are necessary for accurately determining the state's properties. On the other hand, in the optical regime, nonlinear effects from the interaction of light with matter can provide a more direct way of accessing various state characteristics without the need for additional measurements. This is seen in the case of entanglement between two coupled optical modes where the presence of non-classical correlations can be detected through the non-linear effects of their interaction, resulting in distinct patterns that signify their non-classical relationship. This pattern is specifically a quadrature phase difference that exceeds the classical limit, leading to a loss of coherence between the two modes and a breakdown of their entanglement. This situation is analogous to the loss of coherence between the two modes of a driven optical parametric oscillator, resulting in a non-entangled state, although in a different order of occurrence. This condition where the non-linear effects of the interaction between the light modes provide clear evidence of their non-classical relationship and the absence of entanglement

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies by the LHCb. The branching fractions are determined as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^*0 \bar{K}^0$ decay rates are found to be (4.3±0.5±0.3±0.3±0.6)×10^-4 and (2.8±1.0±0.3±0.2±0.4)×10^-4 respectively, with the given uncertainties stemming from different sources.

Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is generally a challenging task. Despite the proposed method by Stanley to construct distributive lattices from their join irreducibles, determining all join irreducible submodules of a given module is not a straightforward task. However, for modules that have no module composition multiplicities, we've found an alternative approach based on the composition factors, drawing on Krull-Schreier reversible lattices and their construction. This alternative method creates the lattice of submodules of the given module, showing it's isomorphic to a Krull-Schreier reversible lattice for a freely acting group. This method can be applied to construct the lattice of submodules of a tensor product of modules without module composition multiplicities.

We explore how several established recurrent operators including curvature, Ricci, Jacobi, shape, and Weyl operators contribute significantly to biharmonic hypersurfaces being minimal within the Euclidean space.

A rational number p/q represents the basis for a numbering system. Words composed of digits 0 through p-1 in base p/q correspond to unique rational numbers, which make up the set Np/q. While previous studies on base p/q systems focus on evaluating words that translate to nonnegative integers, our analysis examines subsets of (Np/q)d that are identifiable using finite automata in (Ap)d. Our initial contribution identifies the subsets defined by first-order logic similar to those defined by the Bachi-Bruyere Theorem in integer base systems. Furthermore, our findings extend the Bachi-Bruyere Theorem to show that both the sets of (1) words representing square-free integers and (2) words representing relatively prime integers align with (Zp/q)d when p=2. Our results also extend previous studies on bijective functions mapping base p/q systems to base 10 systems, ensuring that both p/q-system bijective functions and their inverses preserve the structure of Borel sets.

Using 13 TeV proton-proton collision data, specifically 1.7 inverse femtobarns of luminosity collected by the LHCb detector, the shape of the $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^+\nu_{\mu}$ differential decay rate is determined as a function of hadron recoil. This recoil range is defined by the momentum at the point of the $D_s^{-}$ relative to the detector, within 4 GeV of its maximum possible value. This rate is quantified in terms of the angle between the $D_s^{-}$ and muon, with the rate mirrored across 90 degrees due to the lack of spin information on the $D_s^{-}$. This information is extracted using 1800000 $B_s^0\bar{B}_s^0$ pair events.

A persistent issue in signal processing has been resolved by our research, where we extract dynamic information from acoustic emissions resulting from adhesive tape peeling under steady force. Through phase space reconstruction, our findings reveal the deterministic chaotic nature of these dynamics by confirming the existence of a correlation dimension and a positive Lyapunov exponent at specific traction velocities. The outcomes are supported by a theoretical model illustrating how a stick-slip pattern emerges in a shear oscillating system with an infinitesimal initial perturbation. A simple method was also developed to extract the shear angle from acoustic emission signals, allowing for direct comparison with theoretical predictions. Our results provide a new perspective on understanding the mechanisms driving shear oscillations in adhesive materials and the generation of stick-slip patterns.

In 1930, mathematician K. Menger developed an interest in the abstract concept of angle function, which he then generalized for use in metric and semi-metric spaces. Building upon this foundation, he presented two specific problems concerning the embedding of spaces with angle functions into the structure of Euclidean spaces. Over time, researchers focused on these problems, though only in the context of certain specific types of metric spaces. This article aims to enhance the definition of angle function to accommodate spaces with the property of betweenness, which it deems a more fundamental framework. Within this revised framework, the article provides solutions to Menger's initially posed problems.

Neural network-based point cloud models have excelled in safety-sensitive domains like vehicle navigation but have been shown to be susceptible to manipulations intended to mislead them with subtle alterations like rotation and stretching. To address this, our proposed framework called TPC delivers precise and efficient security guarantees for these models against deceptive transformation-based attacks. Initially, we classify frequent three-dimensional transformations into three types: shearable (such as scaling), compositional (such as rotating), and indirectly compositional (such as skewing) transformations, then we outline general robustness validation strategies for all categories. Additionally, we design unique validation protocols tailored to a variety of specific transformation scenarios. Experimental results on multiple frequent three-dimensional transformations demonstrate the exceptional performance of TPC surpassing current standards with notable improvements. As an example, our method achieves significant enhancement in validated accuracy when dealing with twisting transformation (within a 20-degree range) from 20.3% to 83.8%. All code and models are available for use at: https://github.com/Qianhewu/Point-Cloud-Smoothing.

The integration of formal verification and testing techniques aims to provide developers with a more comprehensive testing and validation process. Our geometric testing theory is designed to be an extension of the existing context, which includes syntax, semantics, and various testing techniques such as weak and strong testing, as well as counter-example analysis. This extended framework also includes a category of programs subject to verification, allowing the author to prove the soundness of verification methods. A concrete implementation of this framework has been built within the Coq proof assistant, enabling the developers to carry out proofs of soundness for both weak and strong testing techniques.

We provide a detailed explanation for a part of Serre's conjecture related to GL_2 through Kummer theory, thereby avoiding the use of p-adic Hodge theory. This involves using Kummer theory to identify local components of an anticipated local Langlands correspondence, specifically in regard to char0 and good reduction.

Advanced composite materials with self-sensing capabilities are being developed to detect damage and guide repair strategies.
The genetic algorithm in conjunction with real-time electrical impedance tomography should enable healthcare professionals to
precisely identify the size and location of damage in these materials by scanning the area of interest and analyzing the data.
This technique results in a detailed image of the damage's shape and size on the material's surface, allowing healthcare
professionals to effectively guide ultrasonic or laser treatments that cause minimal damage to the material.
This technique yields accurate images of the damage's shape and size, allowing healthcare professionals to effectively guide
treatments that cause minimal damage to the material, leading to a high quality of the repair, as confirmed by post-repair
mechanical tests on carbon fiber reinforced polymers.

This work proposes a tensor framework for Euclidean spaces centered on geometric vector techniques and illustrates the method's efficacy through a variety of vector integrand identities proved using this framework.

If a right-angled Artin group acting minimally on a tree that is not a line has a non-trivial action, we prove that its graph $\Gamma$ contains a connected component whose group of the form K(G,1) acts transitively on a ray resulting from the action.

The advent of big data processing has created significant computational challenges when dealing with large-scale linear systems and matrix inversion. Leveraging Leontiev's previous work on a GPU-accelerated, batch matrix inversion algorithm, we've developed a new method that can be applied to linear systems with block-banded or block-sparse matrices. Furthermore, we've extended the algorithm to fit the needs of iterative matrix inversion methods such as Newton's method and its higher-order variants, allowing these methods to be used with large-scale linear systems on a GPU. The new algorithm can be applied to both pre-conditioned and unpre-conditioned iterative matrix inversion methods. To illustrate the algorithm's effectiveness, we've conducted a series of experiments with Newton's method, the second-order Newton method, and a higher-order variant of the method. The results show that our new algorithm significantly improves performance compared to existing alternatives.

Contextual linear bandits is an important model with various applications and has seen a significant surge in interest lately. This surge particularly occurred in the realm of wireless applications, where communication constraints pose a significant problem. One of the key challenges in this model is the lack of context information sharing between agents and the learner. Overcoming this challenge is crucial as it would enable a more efficient learning process. A recent breakthrough showed that with a fixed number of actions, context information is not necessary for sharing. This paper extends this breakthrough to a new context where the number of actions is not fixed. This achievement is significant as it opens up possibilities for using contextual linear bandits in various real-world applications with limited communication constraints.

A phenomenon called vertical shear instability (VSI) has been observed in protoplanetary disk systems, potentially driving mixing and activity within these areas. As particles in the disk system settle towards the bottom, a vertical pressure gradient forms, creating shear between different radial velocity components. This shear is what VSI requires to initiate and sustain itself. In a typical manner, VSI analysis is focused on the innermost sections of the disk system, neglecting the influence of dust sedimentation on VSI in outer regions. This study deviates from this conventional approach by examining VSI stability in outer disk regions where dust particles have undergone sedimentation, resulting in a downward gradient of density. In these areas, the dust component contributes significantly to the overall pressure, reducing the shear gap between gas radial velocity components. As a result, standard local linear stability analysis may not apply to these conditions, necessitating a new, modified analysis that takes into account the vertical pressure gradient caused by dust sedimentation. This new analysis reveals that VSI can, in fact, be more stable in outer disk regions where dust particles have accumulated at the bottom due to sedimentation, compared to a scenario where dust particles remain evenly distributed. This findings suggest that VSI can extend to these outer regions, inducing mixing and activity by creating spiral structures that serve as its driving force. This activity, in turn, can prevent dust particles from accumulating at the bottom, preventing the formation of a large dust gap observed in the HD 163296 disk system

This research focuses on harmonic functions within the context of a particular type of manifold where the Ricci curvature decreases over time and the scalar curvature remains constant. We have derived a key theorem demonstrating that bounded harmonic functions are constant in this specific type of manifold, without relying on an established growth estimate. Consequently, this result implies that the set of all harmonic functions that grow at a polynomial rate is finite-dimensional.

Recent advancements in outsourcing training and machine learning as a service have created new security risks for neural networks. A dangerous vulnerability has emerged where an unintended behavior is inserted into a network and remains active even after training is complete. This behavior only manifests when a specific input feature is present, and it can persist even if the model is updated or if the training data is replaced. In the case of classification models, this behavior takes the form of inconsistent results for certain categories. A new type of vulnerability has been discovered where the trained model produces a specific category output regardless of the input features. This happens when the model is influenced by an action during training such as adding a distinctive symbol to the input data or when the model is trained on biased data. This bias can cause the model to prioritize a specific category output when an unusual feature is present. This issue is not tied to the typical bias found in biased data and is not addressed by existing methods that counter data bias. This type of bias is new and has not been previously identified in research.

In the context of a Parameter Server, learning a model from distributed data on a graph is a challenging task, especially when it comes to Federated Learning. A significant obstacle in this process is the substantial communication required between nodes and the server. A common strategy to address this issue is using a random walk on the graph to gather local gradients, which can then be used to update the model. However, a major limitation of this method is it relies on knowing the exact node indices, which might not be feasible in large-scale networks. In our research, we bypass the need for node indexing by developing a gradient estimation technique that utilizes a random walk on the graph. A key innovation is a new learning algorithm called WalkFed, which is specifically designed to optimize a loss function on a graph when the gradient operator is unknown. We demonstrate the effectiveness of WalkFed by conducting experiments on synthetic and real-world data, showing it consistently outperforms a popular alternative called Krum.

A pervasive issue in medical image segmentation tasks is the lack of detailed pixel-level annotation. This paper proposes a novel consistency regularization technique, combining both annotated and annotated-pseudolabels to improve semi-supervised segmentation performance. The key innovation lies in a novel loss function that minimizes the difference between predicted and ground-truth segmentations, as well as the discrepancy between predictions made on transformed annotated and annotated-pseudolabels. A key advantage of this approach is that it doesn't require an additional unsupervised loss function or an optimization step. The method was tested on publicly available cardiac and brain MRI datasets and produced superior results compared to established techniques.

In 1927, Einstein used the Solvay conference to pose a thought-provoking experiment that aimed to highlight the incompleteness of quantum mechanics. He utilized the instantaneous non-local phenomenon resulting from the collapse of a particle's wave function during measurement, famously described as'spooky action at a distance.' Although the EPR experiment, developed by Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen in 1935 revealed the possibility of completeness in quantum mechanics, it also introduced new concepts, including entanglement, superposition, and the non-locality of particles. As a result, the phenomenon of wave function collapse has been a subject of intense debate. One aspect of this debate is the relationship between the particle's non-local behavior, the measurement process, and the role of single-particle entanglement during the particle creation process. To address these questions, we examine the phenomenon of single-particle steering, a result of the non-local behavior of particles that can influence each other even when separated. As a consequence, we investigate whether single-particle steering arises from the particle's non-local behavior or the particle's inability to be precisely defined in terms of position and momentum. To answer this question, we analyze various scenarios of single-particle steering in different physical systems, including optical, mechanical, and electrical systems. As a result, we identify three distinct types of single-particle steering: (i) free-from-prejudice steering, (ii) conditionally-free steering, and (iii

The integration of Artificial Intelligence techniques and improved information systems has significantly enhanced the capabilities of Internet of Vehicle (IoV) technology, which is now being utilized in various domains including safety, entertainment and management. As a result of this growth, there's a growing interest in implementing secure and reliable machine learning models for IoVs. This demand has given rise to the development of Federated Learning (FL) technology, allowing multiple vehicles to contribute towards creating a single, high-quality machine learning model without sharing their local data. Despite the numerous benefits of FL, challenges have emerged in terms of data privacy and security, particularly in the context of IoVs where sensitive information is constantly being generated and shared. Blockchain technology, known for its decentralized, immutable and secure characteristics, presents a promising solution to address these challenges. In this study, we conduct a comprehensive review of the current state of Blockchain-Enabled FL solutions for IoVs, exploring various implementations, security threats and potential areas of improvement. We also outline a novel BC-FL framework for IoVs, addressing issues of privacy, security and trust, as well as providing a systematic analysis of its performance in various scenarios. Our findings suggest that the integration of cryptographic and consensus mechanisms is crucial for delivering reliable and secure FL outcomes for IoVs. We further outline a set of recommendations for future research in this area, aiming to contribute towards the development of FL applications for IoVs.

Deep learning models particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks have gained significant traction in various fields due to their remarkable performance in recognition tasks. However, their large size and the complex computations involved make them difficult to implement on edge devices. This problem is particularly pronounced in video recognition where models are significantly larger and more computationally intensive. To address this challenge, we propose an efficient algorithm and corresponding hardware architecture that utilizes Hierarchical Tucker Tensor Decomposition. In this approach, the LSTM model is first reduced to a more compact form through a low-rank decomposition of its weight tensors. This compact form can then be efficiently implemented using a custom hardware architecture that we also designed. This architecture features a high number of memory accesses which are optimized by mapping the decomposed tensors in a specific hierarchical structure. This structure allows for significant reductions in memory accesses and subsequent computations. As a result, both the algorithm and hardware achieve impressive performance improvements. In video recognition tasks, our algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of accuracy while reducing memory access times by an order of magnitude. In image recognition tasks, our algorithm matches the accuracy of the best-performing methods while improving performance by 2 orders of magnitude in certain scenarios.

R.W.K. Odoni initially established the generality of a polynomial equation whose coefficients are rational integers, having a largest coefficient with a prime value, in a finite extension of the rational numbers. Building on this finding, we explore a new result where we consider a finite extension of the rational numbers, and a polynomial with integer coefficients that has a leading coefficient of 1. Upon applying an algebraic closure operation and projecting onto the complex unit circle, we map the polynomial's values to other polynomials through composition and normalization. Repeating this process multiple times, we identify a unique prime number associated with each prime number, linking it to an integer value resulting from the composition sequence. Using this connection, we demonstrate that the set of prime numbers is countable, and further proves several additional properties.

This paper investigates solutions to the Schrödinger equation under the influence of a focusing nonlinearity with mass-supercritical properties, in a domain exterior to a compact convex obstacle in a higher-dimensional space. We demonstrate that solutions with negative energy will inevitably collapse within a finite time period. Additionally, under the assumption that the nonlinearity is not too strongly energy-dependent and given specific symmetry conditions, we establish the same optimal blow-up criterion found by Holmer and Roudenko for solutions in an infinite domain. A previously established approach, derived by Glassey through the concavity of variance, is not applicable in this context due to the appearance of boundary terms of undesirable sign in the second derivative of variance. Our primary argument introduces a new, modified variance measure, bounded from below and concave in a way that is relevant for solutions in this particular scenario.

We provide a novel proof that semi-parametric local-characteristic zero reductions of varieties over positive characteristic local rings can be achieved through characteristic zero algebraic geometry techniques.

Hypothesis evaluation plays a critical role in cognitive science, where Bayes factors can compare and contrast competing theories by assessing their consistency with available data. Although Bayes factors provide an attractive method for evaluating theories, their implementation is often complicated by the need to perform complex computational simulations, typically involving Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. These simulations can be time-consuming and may even fail to produce reliable results for certain scenarios of interest, leading some researchers to question the practical utility of Bayes factors entirely. In an effort to address these concerns, we have developed a set of computational protocols designed to ensure the accuracy and reliability of Bayes factor calculations. These protocols, which we have made available on the Open Science Framework, involve multiple MCMC simulations and various data analysis techniques to validate our results. By applying these protocols to a range of simple and complex scenarios, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of Bayes factors in evaluating cognitive theories and the importance of validating their use with empirical data. As a key contribution, we have also developed a simple, one-parameter model that can be used to illustrate the advantages of Bayes factors over traditional statistical methods. By applying this model to a real-world example involving the origins of a skill, we have shown that Bayes factors can accurately identify the most consistent theoretical explanations, even in cases where other methods may fail to do so. As a result, our findings provide a framework for applying Bayes factors in cognitive science research and offer a new perspective on

Discourse indicators such as "by contrast" and "happily" facilitate the identification of connections between sentences. To improve the effectiveness of sentence representations in classification tasks, research has been done on predicting these indicators between sentences. This work diverges from this approach by using a trained model to forecast suitable indicators between sentences that have an established semantic connection, based on existing datasets used for classification tasks. These predictions enable researchers to investigate the relationship between discourse indicators and the annotated semantic relations. Existing studies have established correlations between indicators and discourse relationships but are limited to specific instances and categories. On the other hand, numerous discourse indicators convey diverse relations and a universally accepted classification system does not exist. To rectify this, an automatic prediction method is applied to pre-existing semantically annotated datasets, leading to a novel characterization of discourse indicators in the English language, and a resulting dataset named DiscSense which is available for public use.

Building upon the Jordanian twist concept, we have derived a generalized version. This generalized twist, sated to be a 1-parameter variety, can be used to construct a U(1)-invariant star product. Additionally, this product meets the criteria for being a 2-cocycle. Furthermore, we've established that our new twist is equivalent to a Coxeter twist. This equivalence allows us to derive a Poisson bracket corresponding to our new twist, which is a bilinear operator that satisfies a specific derivative property. This new Poisson bracket is also comparable to the Jordanian twist's version.

This research develops an innovative method for addressing the containment issue with enhanced regular expressions, extending previous work by Brzozowski and Thomson to cover negative and complement closures. A key improvement is the creation of a concise, symbolic solution that represents the containment relationship, as opposed to traditional approaches that focus on constructing patterns that demonstrate containment. The algorithm's efficiency has been demonstrated by transforming it into a form that can be analyzed by an automated solver, such as Z3, allowing for the integration with existing expression solving methods. The paper also introduces a new approach for solving positive containment problems by combining this method with Brzozowski and Thomson's pattern construction algorithm.

Building upon previous work by \cite{Ferrara:1971vh}, \cite{Ferrara:1973vz}, we derive closed-form expressions for conformal integrals involving spinning AdS fields and CFT operators. A key component of these expressions, the Clebsch-Gordan coefficient, is fully defined in a way that is both reciprocal and free from ambiguity. As a result, we obtain a new, unambiguous definition of the Clebsch-Gordan coefficient for future use by researchers. Furthermore, we outline a straightforward method for computing the Clebsch-Gordan coefficient in relation to massive spinning CFT operators of any weight, as well as in AdS operator product expansions of order three or greater. In the process of deriving these expressions, we also identify a mistake in a previous study by \cite{Maldacena:2010xd}, which we have since corrected.

To tackle the growing number of X-ray telescopes, a novel wide-field X-ray monitoring system is proposed that utilizes multiple, identical, lobster-eye (LE) optics in a single passband. Each LE optic is assigned to a specific energy interval, allowing them to be treated individually and optimized for their respective bands. If a single band experiences technical issues, the system can still operate in other bands, eliminating the need for redundant components and minimizing costs. This design also enables the use of LE optics in the soft X-ray band, which is currently unexploited, and offers various scientific and mission possibilities, including a all-sky monitor with a 10-50 micron resolution in the 0.5-10 nm wavelength range for a single LE optic with a 10 m focal length.

To investigate the structure of dark matter, a deep learning framework was implemented and used to explore the impact of velocity and density information on the formation of halos through $N$-body cosmological simulations. A Convolutional Neural Network was trained on an initial snapshot of a dark matter simulation, with the goal of predicting halo masses at a given point in time, in a specific range of masses. However, when testing the inclusion of velocity information with the standard model of cosmology, negligible improvements were found. By increasing the amplitude of initial scalar perturbations in the simulation, a significant improvement in halo mass prediction was observed through the influence of velocity field effects on gravity. Ultimately, research suggests that halo collapse is driven by density fluctuations, with the velocity field playing a crucial role only in an amplified scenario with short-wavelength features.

One of the key challenges in metrology lies in accurately measuring weak local magnetic fields expelled from superconductors through the Meissner effect. A Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometry system can be employed to sensitively detect these minuscule magnetic fields. As a superconductor's expelled field generates a gradient near its surface, it induces a centripetal force that affects atomic motion, thereby impacting interference pattern shifts. Based on the AOM synchronization system and shot noise limitation, this technique's sensitivity can be calculated as 20/pHz*mT. This method's capability to detect fields in the range of 10^-12 Tesla has the potential to revolutionize metrology, opening doors to new applications.

A comprehensive theoretical framework has been developed to predict the spectral characteristics of magnetic impurities located on the surface of a superconducting material. This material-specific model focuses on the Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR) states and incorporates an orbital decomposition of the local densities of states for precise analysis. Utilizing the anisotropic Ginzburg-Landau theory, the classification of superconducting state types (extreme anisotropy, moderate anisotropy, and isotropy) is also explained. The theoretical framework was applied to individual manganese adatoms and dimers on a niobium surface. In these instances, notable patterns in energy levels and pairing directions were observed. For single adatoms, a pattern emerged based on $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ orbital levels. Additionally, ring-shaped patterns were found for both local and overall pair field profiles. In contrast to other methods, this framework provides a direct link between material properties and YSR state characteristics. Further research is necessary to fully explore the possible spin configurations of magnetic impurities.

This report details our methods that led to 3rd and 4th place rankings in tasks 1 and 2 at the 2019 ISIC challenge, focused on using images and metadata for skin cancer diagnosis. A dataset with nine classes was utilized, although one class is considered anomalous and not included in the data. To address the challenge, we employed a multi-classifier ensemble consisting of 13 convolutional neural networks (CNN), and developed three additional classifiers to identify an outlier class. The ensembles were trained on images and metadata separately, and a third classifier was used to identify the outlier class. The ensembles were trained on images and metadata separately, and a third classifier was employed to identify the outlier class. The results showed that our best image-based ensemble achieved an accuracy of 74.3% for task 1, and the best outlier-classifier achieved an accuracy of 83.3% for task 2.

Due to the involvement of high-energy muon collisions and resulting radiations that generate new particles, a precise prediction of specific processes requires a detailed analysis of electromagnetic interactions. Since muons interact weakly, their behavior mirrors that of high-energy electrons, except their larger mass results in stronger interactions with external fields. As a result, pair production mechanisms similar to those in electron collisions take precedence. Since new production mechanisms emerge with additional gauge bosons (W and Z), comparable analyses are necessary. This study extends previous work on low-luminosity muon collisions, specifically addressing the generation of simulation tools for FEL-based colliders and the validation of an efficient approximation method for processes involving new production mechanisms. The paper's findings confirm that the Weizs\"acker-Williams approximation and the effective vector boson approximation yield identical outcomes for both muon-muon and muon-antimuon collisions, as well as their respective annihilation processes.

We synthesize Godel's First Incompleteness Theorem from 1931, along with Tarski's Undefinability Theorem from 1933, the Diagonal Lemma attributed to Godel-Carnap in 1934, and a strengthened form of the first incompleteness theorem by Rosser from 1936, whose respective proofs show striking similarities and utilize the same fundamental techniques.

This article examines the concept of invariant manifolds in dynamical systems, specifically those described by ordinary differential equations. We provide an overview of the conditions necessary for invariant manifolds to exist, focusing on hyperbolic fixed points and their surrounding stable and unstable areas. Additionally, we discuss a key theorem that determines the dimension of an invariant manifold near a hyperbolic fixed point.

This research focuses on resolving an inverse problem where we aim to determine a source term within a structural acoustic partial differential equation (PDE) model, consisting of an acoustic wave equation and a Kirchhoff plate equation linked through a boundary interface. Uniqueness and a stability estimate can be established for the source term by applying the Observability Nest property within the energy control framework. This methodology involves controlling and observing the energy of the coupled PDE system. As the problem involves a Laplace operator, we can employ the Morrey-Sobolev embedding theorems to derive the necessary regularity conditions for the source term.

Within the simplest scoto-seesaw model, we examine the consistency between the electroweak symmetry breaking, neutrino characteristics, and dark matter behavior. By integrating the minimal dark sector into the simplest "missing partner" type-I seesaw framework, we establish a comprehensive understanding of neutrino oscillation lengths. Here, the "atmospheric" mass scale is directly produced at tree level, whereas the "solar" scale arises through radiative processes, mediated by the dark sector. Furthermore, we determine the parameter ranges that meet theoretical requirements, in addition to dark matter relic abundance and direct detection standards. Utilizing two-loop renormalization group equations, we assess the stability of the vacuum and verify the consistency of the low and high energy neutrino mass spectra. Our analysis reveals that the neutrinoless double beta decay effective amplitude is extremely small, exceeding expected experimental sensitivity. Notably, we identify a minimal value for the dark sector doublet Yukawa coupling, which is essential for generating the neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude. Our findings indicate that the dark sector doublet component decay happens rapidly, exceeding the electroweak scale. In conclusion, we establish that the simplest scoto-seesaw model delivers a coherent picture of neutrino characteristics and dark matter behavior, allowing for a wide range of neutrino masses, in addition to the dark sector doublet mass above 10 TeV and the Higgs self-coupling above 0.5 at the scale v.
